summary: Umar rebukes a man who built with baked bricks, warning that people like Fir'oun could appear in this Ummah.
Saalim bin Abdullaah bin Umar recounts how Abu Ayyoob rebuked his father Abdullaah for decorating the walls at Saalim's wedding, and refused to enter the house or eat there.
Salmaan Faarsi asks Abu Bakr for advice, and Abu Bakr counsels him to fear Allaah, take only what he needs, keep the five salaahs, and never wrong anyone under Allaah's protection.
Hasan reports that Salmaan Faarsi visited Abu Bakr on his deathbed for advice, and Abu Bakr said Allaah will open the world, so no one should take more than he needs.
notes: 'Hadhrat Hasan' is not identified in the text; left unlinked, so it could be Hasan al-Basri or another narrator.

summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf visits the dying Abu Bakr, who warns that worldly wealth is coming and that being executed is better for a person than drowning in the intoxication of this world.
Amr bin Al Aas rebukes his companions for craving the world the Prophet avoided, saying the Prophet never had more than he owed.
notes: The narrator's first name is lost to OCR ('Hadhrat (RA) bin Rabaah'). Left unlinked rather than matched to the approved 'rabaah' (unsure).

summary: Amr bin Al Aas says the Prophet never went three days without his debts exceeding his dues, and contrasts the Prophet's abstinence with the Companions' desire for the world.
notes: Two variant sayings of Amr, joined as one narration.

summary: When his son asked for a new garment, Abdullaah bin Umar told him to cut off the torn part and wear the rest, and warned against living only for food and clothing.
Abu Dharr rebukes Abu Dardaa for building a house, saying he is loading boulders onto people's necks, and says he would have preferred to see him tending his family's waste.
notes: 'Hadhrat Thaabit' is linked to the approved Thaabit Bunaani; the text gives no further name.

summary: Aa'isha wore a new garment and Abu Bakr warned that Allaah dislikes a servant who admires himself for worldly beauty, so she gave the garment away as sadaqah.
notes: The text is cut off mid-sentence ('That shall perhaps atone for').

summary: Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah kills his father during the Battle of Badr after he kept confronting him, and Allaah reveals the verse that believers do not befriend those who oppose Allaah and His Rasool, even their fathers.
new_themes: disassociation from kin who oppose Islaam
notes: The text names only 'Abu Ubaydah' and gives no patronymic; linked to the approved Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah. The father is not named. The verse quote is partly garbled by OCR.

summary: Maalik bin Umayr reports two men who fought or left their fathers in battle, and the Prophet stayed silent; Abu Hurayrah reports that Abdullaah bin Ubay's son offered to bring his father's head, and the Prophet refused.
new_themes: disassociation from kin who oppose Islaam
notes: Two separate reports: Maalik bin Umayr's account of the two men, and Abu Hurayrah's account of Abdullaah bin Ubay.

summary: Abdullaah, son of Abdullaah bin Ubay, asks the Prophet for permission to execute his father, and the Prophet refuses, choosing to be lenient with him while he remains among the Muslims.
notes: Two narrations of one episode (the son's own account and Aasim's variant), kept as one.

summary: Usaama bin Zaid reports that Abdullaah, son of Abdullaah bin Ubay, drew his sword before his father and vowed not to sheathe it until his father called the Prophet honourable; the Prophet was pleased with his act.
Urwa reports that Handhala, son of Abu Aamir, and Abdullaah, son of Abdullaah bin Ubay, both asked the Prophet to let them execute their fathers, and he refused.
new_themes: disassociation from kin who oppose Islaam
notes: Urwa is linked to the approved Urwa bin Zubayr by name only (approved as unsure); the text gives no patronymic.

summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr tells his father he avoided him at Uhud, and Abu Bakr says he would have attacked him; later, when the still non-Muslim Abdur Rahmaan challenged for a duel, Abu Bakr stood up to accept and the Prophet held him back.
notes: Two separate reports: the Uhud exchange with his father, and Waaqidi's report of the duel challenge. The text places the first exchange at Uhud while the heading says Badr.

summary: Umar tells Sa'eed bin Al Aas that he did not kill Sa'eed's father, who was struck down by Ali after Umar turned away, and Sa'eed replies that his father was on falsehood; Umar is greatly pleased.
notes: The approved list marks Sa'eed bin Al Aas as 'no' but the text gives him (RA); linked to the approved id as given. The narrator 'Abu Ubaydah' is not identified with a patronymic, so left unlinked. Second paragraph is a variant of Sa'eed's reply.

summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet spoke to the Mushrikeen dragged into a well after Badr, and Abu Hudhayfah grieved over his father Utba being dragged there; the Prophet made dua for him.
new_themes: disassociation from kin who oppose Islaam
notes: Covers the well incident (Aa'isha), Abu Hudhayfah's reaction, and a separate Abu Zinaad report of his duel challenge and Hind's couplets.

summary: Nubay bin Wahab reports the Prophet ordered Badr captives treated well; Abu Azeez, Mus'ab's captive brother, recounts that the Ansaar gave him bread, and that Mus'ab told his captor to bind him tightly because his mother would pay a ransom.
notes: Same episode as n01300, told with different wording.

summary: Ayyoob bin Nu'maan reports the same episode: Mus'ab asked Muhriz to bind Abu Azeez tightly for ransom, Abu Azeez protested, and his mother then paid four thousand dirhams.
notes: Repeats the episode in n01299 with different wording.

summary: Zuhri reports that Abu Sufyaan, before accepting Islaam, asked the Prophet to extend the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and was refused; he then sat down on the Prophet's bedding, and his daughter Ummu Habeebah rolled it up.
Ummu Habeebah adds that she did not want her father to sit on the Prophet's bedding.
notes: A short variant that continues n01301.

summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says he would rather dust the sand from his sons' graves than see a sparrow's egg fall from its nest, and that he would rather his family die and he follow them than see the sparrow die.
notes: Two separate reports: Abul Ahwas's account of the visit, and Abu Uthmaan's account in Kufa of the sparrow soiling him.

summary: Umar, disagreeing with Abu Bakr about the Badr prisoners, asks that Aqeel be handed to Ali and Abbaas to Hamza for execution, so Allaah would know the Muslims have no love for the Mushrikeen; the passage ends with an author's note on the Ansaar.
new_themes: disassociation from kin who oppose Islaam
notes: Opens with the author's cross-reference 'The narration has already passed' and ends mid-sentence ('during the Period of').

summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr reports that Sa'd bin Mu'aadh offered to build the Prophet a shelter at Badr so he could stay safe, and the Prophet praised him and prayed for him.
notes: The approved list has 'Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr' twice (abdullaah-bin-abi-bakr and abdullaah-bin-abu-bakr, both yes); the spelling in this text matches abdullaah-bin-abu-bakr.

summary: Aa'isha reports a man who feared he would not see the Prophet in Jannah; Allaah revealed Nisaa verse 69, promising companionship with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous.
Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports a man who loved the Prophet and feared he would be on a lower level in Jannah; Allaah revealed Nisaa verse 69, and the Prophet recited it to him.

Anas reports that a man asked when Qiyaamah would come and said he had prepared only his love for Allaah and His Rasool; the Prophet told him he would be with those he loves, and Anas says he loves the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar.

A man from the desert asks when Qiyaamah will come and says he loves Allaah and His Rasool; the Prophet tells him he will be with those he loves, and Anas says the Companions were overjoyed. A Tirmidhi report adds a similar exchange.
notes: Two separate reports of the same saying: one attributed to Bukhaari and one to Tirmidhi.

summary: Abu Dharr asks the Prophet about a man who loves a people but cannot do their deeds; the Prophet tells Abu Dharr he will be with those he loves, and Abu Dharr says he loves Allaah and His Rasool.
notes: The text stops mid-sentence ('repeated what he had )').

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Ali earned dates for the hungry Prophet by drawing water for a Jewish man; the Prophet told him that love for Allaah brings hardship. Talha then dies before the Prophet arrives, and the Prophet prays that he be smiling when he meets Allaah.
notes: Two events in one report: Ali's dates and the death of Talha bin Ubaydillaah.

summary: Talha bin Miskeen reports that Talha bin Baraa pledged to the Prophet only after being told Islaam does not require severing ties with parents; Talha later fell ill and died, and the Prophet prayed for him.
notes: Talha bin Baraa is distinct from the approved Talha bin Ubaydillaah.

summary: Zuhri reports that someone complained to the Prophet about Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa's jokes and useless talk, and the Prophet told them to leave him because his heart loves Allaah and His Rasool.

Adra reports that a man reciting Qur'aan loudly at night was called a show-off, and the Prophet said he was Abdullaah bin Dhul Bijaadayn; after his burial the Prophet widened the grave, and mourned him because of his love for Allaah and His Rasool.
notes: The text does not give Abdullaah bin Dhul Bijaadayn the (RA) title; marked yes as a Companion from outside the text.

summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Sa'd reports that Abdullaah bin Umar's cramp eased when he named the Prophet, and recalls Zaid bin Dathana and Khubayb bin Adi refusing to let the Prophet be harmed even to save their own lives.
notes: Starts with a cross-reference to an earlier story and ends mid-title (the chapter name is cut off).

summary: Anas and Abdullaah bin Umar report that Abu Bakr wept when his father Abu Quhaafah came to pledge to the Prophet, having hoped Abu Taalib would accept Islaam instead; Abu Bakr told the Prophet that his happiness is all he wishes for.
notes: Two separate reports: Anas on the pledge, and Abdullaah bin Umar on Abu Bakr leading his father to the Prophet at the conquest of Makkah.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar offering to free the captive Abbaas from the Ansaar, who refused; the Prophet was troubled, so the Companions began informing him only after a death, and later carried biers to his house. Umar bin Muhammad explains the place Mowda'ul Janaa'iz is named after this practice.
notes: Several parts: Ibn Umar's account of Abbaas's captivity, a report on the funeral-prayer practice, and Umar bin Muhammad's note on the place.

summary: Aslam reports that Umar went to Faatima, the Prophet's daughter, and told her that after her father none was dearer to him.
Anas reports that the Companions did not raise their gaze before the Prophet, except Abu Bakr and Umar, who were close enough to smile and speak informally with him.

Usaama bin Shareek describes the Companions sitting so still around the Prophet that it seemed birds were perched on their backs, and the Prophet said the most beloved servants of Allaah are those with the best character.
notes: The second paragraph is a variant of the same scene.
